title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law of the People's Republic of China (II)

articles.content_en: Except for the debtor's own currency and tangible objects, the claims, stock rights, intellectual property rights, usufruct, and other property and property rights and interests that the debtor enjoys according to law and that may be valued in currency and transferred according to law shall all be recognized by the People's Court as debtor's property.

The specific property of the debtor on which a security interest has been created according to law shall be recognized by the People's Court as debtor's property.
The remaining portion, after the extinguishment of the security interest or the realization of the security interest, of the debtor's specific property may be used in the bankruptcy proceedings to pay bankruptcy expenses, common benefit debts, and other bankruptcy claims.

The relevant share of the debtor in co-owned property owned in shares, or the corresponding property rights in co-owned property owned jointly, and the portion obtained from dividing co-owned property according to law shall all be recognized by the People's Court as debtor's property.
Where the People's Court declares the debtor's bankruptcy liquidation, this constitutes a statutory cause for division of co-owned property. Where the People's Court rules for reorganization or composition of the debtor, the division of co-owned property shall be conducted in accordance with Article 303 of the Civil Code; where the co-owned property must be divided due to the needs of reorganization or composition, and the administrator requests division, the People's Court shall permit it.
Where debts arise from damage caused to other co-owners due to the division of co-owned property, and the other co-owners request discharge as common benefit debts, the People's Court shall support it.

After the acceptance of a bankruptcy application, where the execution procedures concerning the debtor's property have not been suspended in accordance with Article 19 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, the relevant unit that took execution measures shall make corrections according to law. Property returned through execution in accordance with law shall be recognized by the People's Court as debtor's property.

After the acceptance of a bankruptcy application, where the lawful conduct of the bankruptcy proceedings may be affected by the acts of relevant interested parties or for other reasons, the People's Court that accepted the bankruptcy application may, upon the administrator's application or ex officio, take preservation measures against all or part of the debtor's property.

The relevant unit that has taken preservation measures against the debtor's property shall, upon learning that the People's Court has ruled to accept the bankruptcy application concerning the debtor, promptly release the preservation measures against the debtor's property in accordance with Article 19 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law.

Where the People's Court, after accepting a bankruptcy application but before declaring bankruptcy, rules to reject the bankruptcy application, or rules to terminate the bankruptcy proceedings pursuant to Article 108 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, it shall promptly notify the unit that originally took preservation measures and has released them according to law to restore the relevant preservation measures in accordance with the original preservation priority.
Before the unit that has released the preservation measures according to law restores them or indicates that it does not intend to restore them, the People's Court that accepted the bankruptcy application shall not release the preservation measures against the debtor's property.

Where the administrator initiates a lawsuit pursuant to Articles 31 and 32 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, requesting the revocation of relevant acts involving the debtor's property and the return of the debtor's property by the counterparty, the People's Court shall support it.
Where the administrator, due to fault, fails to exercise the right of revocation according to law, causing improper diminution of the debtor's property, and a creditor initiates a lawsuit claiming that the administrator bears corresponding liability for compensation for its losses, the People's Court shall support it.

Where the debtor is transferred into bankruptcy proceedings after administrative liquidation procedures, the starting point for computing the revocable acts provided in Articles 31 and 32 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law shall be the date on which the administrative supervision authority makes the revocation decision.
Where the debtor is transferred into bankruptcy proceedings after compulsory liquidation procedures, the starting point for computing the revocable acts provided in Articles 31 and 32 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law shall be the date on which the People's Court rules to accept the compulsory liquidation application.

Where the People's Court revokes, upon the administrator's request, a transaction involving the debtor's property conducted at a clearly unreasonable price, the buyer and seller shall return to each other the property or price obtained from the other party according to law.
Where, due to the revocation of such transaction, the debtor owes a debt arising from returning the price already paid by the transferee, and the transferee requests discharge as a common benefit debt, the People's Court shall support it.

Where a debtor makes early payment of an undue debt within one year before the acceptance of the bankruptcy application, and the debt has already become due before the acceptance of the bankruptcy application, and the administrator requests revocation of such payment, the People's Court shall not support it. However, this is excepted where such payment occurred within six months before the acceptance of the bankruptcy application and the debtor has the circumstances provided in Article 2, Paragraph 1 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law.

After the acceptance of a bankruptcy application, where the administrator fails to request, pursuant to Article 31 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, revocation of the debtor's acts of gratuitously transferring property, transacting at a clearly unreasonable price, or relinquishing claims, and a creditor initiates a lawsuit pursuant to Articles 538 and 539 of the Civil Code, requesting revocation of the above acts of the debtor and the inclusion of the recovered property into the debtor's property, the People's Court shall accept it.
Where the counterparty defends on the ground that the scope of the creditor's exercise of the right of revocation exceeds the creditor's claim, the People's Court shall not support it.

Where the debtor makes individual repayment of a claim secured by a security interest created on its own property, and the administrator requests revocation pursuant to Article 32 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, the People's Court shall not support it. However, this is excepted where the value of the secured property at the time of repayment is lower than the amount of the claim.

Where the debtor makes individual repayment to a creditor through litigation, arbitration, or execution procedures, and the administrator requests revocation pursuant to Article 32 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, the People's Court shall not support it. However, this is excepted where the debtor and the creditor maliciously collude to harm the interests of other creditors.

Where the administrator initiates a lawsuit pursuant to Article 33 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, claiming that the actual possessor of concealed or transferred property returns the debtor's property, or claiming that the debtor's act of fabricating debts or acknowledging unreal debts is void and that the property is returned to the debtor, the People's Court shall support it.

Where the administrator, representing the debtor, initiates a lawsuit pursuant to Article 128 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law on the grounds that the debtor's legal representative and other directly responsible persons have intentional or gross negligence in the relevant acts concerning the debtor's property, causing losses to the debtor's property, and claims that the aforesaid responsible persons bear corresponding liability for compensation, the People's Court shall support it.

The limitation of action for claims enjoyed by the debtor against third parties shall be interrupted from the date on which the People's Court accepts the bankruptcy application.
Where the debtor, without justifiable reasons, fails to timely exercise its rights with respect to its matured claims, causing its external claims to exceed the limitation period within one year before the acceptance of the bankruptcy application, the limitation period for the aforesaid claims shall be recalculated from the date on which the People's Court accepts the bankruptcy application.

Where the administrator initiates a lawsuit on behalf of the debtor, claiming that a capital contributor shall pay the unfulfilled capital contribution to the debtor according to law or return the capital contribution and its interest withdrawn in violation of law, and the capital contributor defends on the ground that the subscribed capital contribution has not yet matured as required by the company's articles of association, or that the limitation of action has expired with respect to the breach of the capital contribution obligation, the People's Court shall not support the defense.
Where the administrator, pursuant to the relevant provisions of the Company Law, initiates a lawsuit on behalf of the debtor, claiming that the company's promoters and the directors and senior officers who have the duty to supervise shareholders' performance of capital contribution obligations, or other shareholders, directors, senior officers, actual controllers, etc. who assisted in the withdrawal of capital contributions, bear corresponding liability for shareholders' breach of capital contribution obligations or withdrawal of capital contributions, and that the property be turned over to the debtor's property, the People's Court shall support it.

Before the acceptance of a bankruptcy application, where a creditor initiates a lawsuit listed in Article 21, Paragraph 1 of these Provisions against the debtor's property in the People's Court, and the People's Court has already rendered an effective civil judgment or mediation document but the execution has not been completed, after the acceptance of the bankruptcy application, the relevant execution acts shall be suspended pursuant to Article 19 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, and the creditor shall declare the relevant claims to the administrator according to law.

After the acceptance of a bankruptcy application, where a creditor initiates a lawsuit listed in Article 21, Paragraph 1 of these Provisions against the debtor's property in the People's Court, the People's Court shall not accept it.
Where a creditor, through the creditors' meeting or the creditors' committee, requires the administrator to recover debtor's property according to law from the secondary debtor, the debtor's capital contributors, etc., and the administrator refuses to recover without justifiable reasons, and the creditors' meeting applies to the People's Court to replace the administrator pursuant to Article 22 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, the People's Court shall support it.
Where the administrator fails to recover, and individual creditors initiate relevant lawsuits on behalf of all creditors, claiming that the secondary debtor or the debtor's capital contributors etc. pay debts to the debtor or return the debtor's property, or applying for consolidated bankruptcy according to law, the People's Court shall accept it.

Where the administrator intends to take back pledged articles or retained articles by paying off debts or providing security, or to reach an agreement with the pledgee or lien holder to discharge debts by evaluating the pledged articles or retained articles at appraised value, or to conduct any other disposal of property with a material impact on the interests of creditors, it shall promptly report to the creditors' committee. Where no creditors' committee is established, the administrator shall promptly report to the People's Court.

A right holder exercising the right to take back property pursuant to Article 38 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law shall raise it with the administrator before the bankruptcy property realization plan or the composition agreement or draft reorganization plan is submitted to the creditors' meeting for voting. Where the right holder claims to take back the relevant property after the aforesaid period, it shall bear the relevant increased expenses caused by the delayed exercise of the right to take back property.

Where a right holder claims to take back the relevant property from the administrator pursuant to Article 38 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, and the administrator does not approve it, and the right holder initiates a lawsuit in the People's Court against the debtor as defendant requesting to exercise the right to take back property, the People's Court shall accept it.
Where a right holder claims to take back the disputed property from the administrator in accordance with the relevant effective legal documents of the People's Court or arbitration institution, and the administrator refuses to allow the exercise of the right to take back property on the ground that the effective legal document is erroneous, the People's Court shall not support it.

Where a right holder, when exercising the right to take back property, fails to pay the administrator the relevant processing fees, storage fees, freight, agency fees, consignment fees, and other expenses according to law, and the administrator refuses to allow the taking back of the relevant property, the People's Court shall support it.

With respect to property in the possession of the debtor that is of unclear ownership, perishable and difficult to store, or property whose value would seriously depreciate if not promptly realized, where the administrator promptly realizes the property and deposits the realization proceeds, and the relevant right holder exercises the right to take back property with respect to such realization proceeds, the People's Court shall support it.

Where property of others in the possession of the debtor is damaged or destroyed, and the insurance money, compensation, or replacement obtained therefrom has not yet been delivered to the debtor, or although the replacement has been delivered to the debtor, it can be distinguished from the debtor's property, and the right holder claims to take back the insurance money, compensation, or replacement so obtained, the People's Court shall support it.
Where the insurance money or compensation has been delivered to the debtor, or the replacement has been delivered to the debtor and cannot be distinguished from the debtor's property, the People's Court shall handle the matter in accordance with the following provisions:
(1) if the damage or destruction occurred before the acceptance of the bankruptcy application, the claim formed by the right holder due to property loss shall be discharged as an ordinary bankruptcy claim;
(2) if the damage or destruction occurred after the acceptance of the bankruptcy application, the debt arising from damage to the right holder due to the administrator's or relevant personnel's performance of duties shall be discharged as a common benefit debt.
Where property of others in the possession of the debtor is damaged or destroyed, and no corresponding insurance money, compensation, or replacement is obtained, or the insurance money, compensation, or replacement is insufficient to cover the loss, the People's Court shall handle it in accordance with Paragraph 2 of this Article.

Where, in the course of performing duties, the administrator or relevant personnel improperly transfer another person's property or cause damage or destruction of another person's property due to intentional or gross negligence, and the debt arising from damage to others is a common benefit debt, if the debtor's property is insufficient to compensate the loss, and the right holder claims that the administrator or relevant personnel bear supplementary liability for compensation, the People's Court shall support it.
After the aforesaid debt has been paid at any time from the debtor's property as a common benefit debt, if a creditor initiates a lawsuit on the ground that the improper performance of duties by the administrator or relevant personnel caused a reduction of the debtor's property and resulting losses to the creditor, and claims that the administrator or relevant personnel bear corresponding liability for compensation, the People's Court shall support it.

Where the parties to a sales contract agree in the contract to retain title to the subject matter, and before the ownership of the subject matter is transferred to the buyer according to law, one party goes bankrupt, the sales contract shall be a contract for which both parties have not completed performance, and the administrator has the right to decide, pursuant to Article 18 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, to rescind or continue to perform the contract.

Where the seller goes bankrupt and its administrator decides to continue performing the sales contract with retention of title, the buyer shall pay the price or perform other obligations in accordance with the original sales contract.
Where the buyer fails to pay the price or complete other obligations in accordance with the contract, or sells, pledges, or otherwise improperly disposes of the subject matter, causing damage to the seller, and the seller's administrator claims to take back the subject matter according to law, the People's Court shall support it. However, this is excepted where the buyer has paid 75% or more of the total price of the subject matter or a third party has acquired ownership or other real rights in the subject matter in good faith.
Where the subject matter cannot be taken back due to the circumstances in Paragraph 2 of this Article, and the seller's administrator claims according to law that the buyer continue to pay the price, complete other obligations, and bear corresponding liability for compensation, the People's Court shall support it.

Where the seller goes bankrupt and its administrator decides to rescind the sales contract with retention of title and, pursuant to Article 17 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, requires the buyer to deliver the subject matter to it, the People's Court shall support it.
Where the buyer defends on the ground that there are no circumstances such as failure to pay the price or complete other obligations in accordance with the contract, or selling, pledging, or otherwise improperly disposing of the subject matter, the People's Court shall not support it.
After the buyer lawfully performs the contract obligations and delivers the subject matter to the seller's administrator in accordance with Paragraph 1 of this Article, the claim formed by the buyer's loss of the price paid shall be discharged as a common benefit debt. However, where the buyer violates the contract, and the seller's administrator claims that the aforesaid claim be discharged as an ordinary bankruptcy claim, the People's Court shall support it.

Article 37 Where the buyer enters bankruptcy, and its administrator decides to continue performing the retention-of-title sales contract, the time limit for the buyer to pay the price or perform other obligations as agreed in the original sales contract shall be deemed to have become due upon acceptance of the bankruptcy application, and the buyer's administrator shall promptly pay the price or perform other obligations to the seller.
Where the buyer's administrator, without justifiable reasons, fails to pay the price or fully perform other obligations in a timely manner, or sells, pledges, or otherwise improperly disposes of the subject matter, causing damage to the seller, and the seller claims to reclaim the subject matter pursuant to Article 641 of the Civil Code and other provisions, the People's Court shall support it. However, this does not apply where the buyer has paid not less than 75% of the total price of the subject matter or where a third party has acquired ownership or other real rights in the subject matter in good faith.
Where the subject matter cannot be reclaimed due to the circumstances specified in the second paragraph of this Article, and the seller, in accordance with law, claims that the buyer shall continue to pay the price, fully perform other obligations, and bear corresponding liability for compensation, the People's Court shall support it. With respect to the debts arising from the damage caused to the seller by the buyer's failure to pay the price or fully perform other obligations, and by the buyer's administrator's sale, pledge, or other improper disposal of the subject matter, where the seller claims that they shall be satisfied as common benefit debts, the People's Court shall support it.

Article 38 Where the buyer enters bankruptcy, and its administrator decides to rescind the retention-of-title sales contract, and the seller claims to reclaim the sold subject matter pursuant to Article 38 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, the People's Court shall support it.
Where the seller reclaims the sold subject matter, and the buyer's administrator claims that the seller shall return the price already paid, the People's Court shall support it. Where the value of the reclaimed subject matter has obviously decreased, causing losses to the seller, the seller may, after deducting such losses from the price already paid by the buyer on a priority basis, return the remaining amount to the buyer; where the price already paid by the buyer is insufficient to cover the loss caused to the seller by the decrease in the value of the subject matter, and the seller claims that the debt shall be satisfied as a common benefit debt, the People's Court shall support it.

Article 39 Where the seller, pursuant to Article 39 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, claims the right of reclamation over the subject matter in transit but fails to realize it through such means as notifying the carrier or actual possessor to suspend transportation, return the goods, change the destination, or deliver the goods to another consignee, or has already claimed the reclamation of the subject matter in transit from the administrator before the goods arrived at the administrator, after the sold subject matter arrives at the administrator, if the seller claims reclamation from the administrator, the administrator shall permit it.
Where the seller fails to timely exercise the right of reclamation over the subject matter in transit, and after the sold subject matter arrives at the administrator, the seller exercises the right of reclamation over the subject matter in transit with the administrator, the administrator shall not permit it.

Article 40 During the reorganization period of the debtor, where a right holder requests the return of its property lawfully possessed by the debtor, and such request does not conform to the conditions previously agreed upon by both parties, the People's Court shall not support it. However, this does not apply where the administrator or the debtor in self-management violates the agreement, which may cause the property to be reclaimed to be transferred, damaged, destroyed, or significantly reduced in value.

Article 41 Where a creditor exercises the right of set-off pursuant to Article 40 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, it shall submit a set-off claim to the administrator.
The administrator shall not proactively set off the mutual debts between the debtor and the creditor, except where the set-off benefits the debtor's estate.

Article 42 After receiving the notice from the creditor claiming set-off of debts, if the administrator, upon examination, has no objection, the set-off shall take effect from the date the administrator receives the notice.
Where the administrator has objection to the set-off claim, it shall initiate litigation in the People's Court within the agreed objection period or within three months from the date of receiving the notice claiming set-off of debts. Where the litigation is filed late without justifiable reasons, the People's Court shall not support it.
Where the People's Court renders a judgment rejecting the administrator's claim for invalidation of the set-off, the set-off shall take effect from the date the administrator received the notice claiming set-off of debts.

Article 44 Within the six months before the acceptance of the bankruptcy application, where the debtor is in the circumstances prescribed in Article 2, Paragraph 1 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, and the debtor, by way of set-off with an individual creditor, makes repayment to that individual creditor, and the claims and debts set off fall under one of the circumstances prescribed in items (2) and (3) of Article 40 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, if the administrator, within three months from the date of acceptance of the bankruptcy application, initiates litigation in the People's Court claiming that the set-off is invalid, the People's Court shall support it.

Article 45 Where a creditor falling under the circumstances where set-off is not permitted as listed in Article 40 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law claims to set off its claim that enjoys a right to priority satisfaction against the debtor's specific property with the debt owed by it to the debtor that does not enjoy a right to priority satisfaction, and the debtor's administrator raises objection on the ground that the set-off involves circumstances prescribed in Article 40 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, the People's Court shall not support the objection. However, this does not apply where the claim used for set-off exceeds the value of the property over which the creditor enjoys the right to priority satisfaction.

Article 47 After a People's Court accepts a bankruptcy application, civil action cases concerning the debtor brought by parties shall, pursuant to Article 21 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court that accepted the bankruptcy application.
First-instance civil cases concerning the debtor under the jurisdiction of the People's Court that accepted the bankruptcy application may, pursuant to Article 38 of the Civil Procedure Law, be brought up for trial by a higher People's Court, or submitted to a higher People's Court for approval and then referred to a lower People's Court for trial.
Where the People's Court that accepted the bankruptcy application cannot exercise jurisdiction over cases such as maritime disputes, patent disputes, or civil compensation disputes arising from misrepresentation in the securities market concerning the debtor, it may, pursuant to Article 37 of the Civil Procedure Law, have jurisdiction designated by a higher People's Court.

Article 48 Where judicial interpretations on enterprise bankruptcy issued by this Court before the implementation of these Provisions are inconsistent with these Provisions, they shall no longer apply from the date these Provisions come into force.
